**[SafeAI.watch](https://safeai.watch)** is a public record of AI safety and security for general readers: research, reported incidents, public warnings and policy responses. Each entry links its original source, gives its key points, and separates what happened from what the evidence shows.

The record holds 388 entries from Mar 22, 2023 to Oct 30, 2026 (79 warnings, 91 incidents, 107 governance, 111 research), drawn from 211 publishers. It is a selection, not a complete count: the burst above shows what the record covers, so its dense rim is no measure of how often such events happen. Read it on the site: [Latest](https://safeai.watch/latest), [Timeline](https://safeai.watch/timeline), [About](https://safeai.watch/about).

## How an entry reads

Every entry sets out what happened, the source's key points and what the evidence shows, and adds what remains uncertain when something material is still open. The newest one, from Oct 30, 2026, filed under Governance:

> **OpenAI says it made over 200 law enforcement referrals in Q3 and will let ChatGPT end chats fixated on violence**
>
> **What happened.** OpenAI announced on October 30, 2026 that it will publish a Community Safety Report and add ChatGPT safeguards against violence, with further limits for teens.
>
> **Key points.**
>
> - As part of bringing imminent threats of violence to law enforcement, OpenAI says "we made over 200 law enforcement referrals in Q3 2026."
> - The first report, covering the second half of 2026, is due in early 2027 and every six months after, with anonymized examples and data on its safeguards.
> - For all users, ChatGPT will restrict reconstructions of past mass attacks; when a user fixates on violence it can end the chat, and repeated endings may pause the account.
> - Teens face new limits on practical information about weapons and security systems even without signs of violent intent.
>
> **Evidence.** Company post announcing policy changes and a future report. The referral count is OpenAI's own figure, given without a breakdown.
>
> **Uncertain.** The safeguards had not yet launched; OpenAI says they "will begin rolling out in the next few weeks."
>
> **Source.** [OpenAI · Company post](https://openai.com/index/community-safety-report-and-new-protections-for-teens/)

## Run it locally

Needs Node.js 22.12.0 or later.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev
```

The dev server runs at http://localhost:4321. `npm run build` writes the static site to `dist/`, and `npm run preview` serves that build. The build first runs `npm run film:lint`, which checks the About page film's script against its facts.

## Add or correct an entry

Entries live in [`src/data/events.json`](src/data/events.json). Each one has exactly these keys: `date` (the source's publication date, `YYYY-MM-DD`), `category` (one of `"Warnings"`, `"Incidents"`, `"Governance"`, `"Research"`), `topics` (one to three different subjects from `"Bio"`, `"Cyber"`, `"Rogue agents"`, `"Alignment"`, `"Superintelligence"`, `"Harm to people"`, `"Military"`, `"Lab conduct"`, most central first), `title`, `happened`, `keyPoints` (a list of one to four short points), `evidence`, `source` (publisher and source type, such as "RAND · Research report") and `url` (https only), plus an optional `uncertain`. [`src/data/days.json`](src/data/days.json) holds a brief of one or two sentences for every date with three or more entries, and only for those dates; on a date with six or more entries the brief also names that day's five most significant entries. The rules for choosing topics and writing briefs are in the [add-source topics reference](.claude/skills/add-source/references/topics.md). [`src/data/record.ts`](src/data/record.ts) checks every entry and brief when the site builds and fails the build on a missing, empty or extra key, an empty or overlong `keyPoints` list, an unknown category, an empty `topics` list or one with more than three, repeated or unknown topics, a date not written as `YYYY-MM-DD`, a link that is not https, or a missing, stray or malformed day brief. Run `npm run build` to check a change; CI runs the same build on every pull request.

The art above is generated from the same file. After changing the record, run `node scripts/readme/build.mjs` and commit `README.md` and `assets/readme/` with it; CI fails while they are out of date. Changes land through pull requests, and a merge to `main` deploys the site.

Spotted an error in an entry? [Open an issue](https://github.com/ryanportfolio/SafeAI.Watch/issues) with the entry's title and a source that shows the correction.

## What the project holds to

- Every entry links its original source.
- Each entry gives the source's key points and separates what happened from what the evidence shows, with what remains uncertain when something material is still open.
- No invented incidents, numbers or quotes. The site's illustrations are conceptual and carry no data; the chart at the top of this README is the exception, drawn from the record.
- No third-party trackers or analytics.

## Layout

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `src/pages/` | The site's pages, built by [Astro](https://astro.build) as static HTML |
| `src/data/` | The record and its build-time checks |
| `src/scripts/visuals/` | The homepage's WebGL visuals |
| `src/scripts/film/`, `film/` | The About page film and its script |
| `scripts/film/` | The film's script check (`npm run film:lint`) and video export |
| `scripts/brand/` | The logo, icons and font subset (`npm run brand`) |
| `scripts/readme/` | This README and its art |
